Annual work programme
2026
European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive
Agency (EISMEA)
1

FOREWORD. Message from the Director
In 2026, EISMEA will continue to support the political priorities of its parent DGs by implementing
ambitious programmes that aim to drive forward competitiveness and innovation with a strong
focus on start-ups and SMEs.
Pioneering transformative innovation
The agency will launch a new pilot EIC Advanced Innovation Challenges under Horizon Europe to
support high-risk, demand-driven deep tech innovation with transformative potential, while
continuing to manage calls under the EIC Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP) to
stimulate groundbreaking innovation in strategic technologies.
The annual EIC Summit on 3-4 June 2026 will showcase tangible evidence of the EIC’s impact,
cementing the programme’s place in the heart of the European deep-tech eco-system.
Scaling up innovation across regions
EISMEA will support the EU’s startup and scaleups strategy through both the EIC and European
Innovation Ecosystems (EIE), with the latter launching calls centred on competitiveness-driven
topics, including the European startup and scaleup hubs pilot. At the same time, the agency
continues to provide support for Ukrainian tech SMEs and startups.
Supporting the New European Innovation Agenda, the agency will continue implementing the
Regional Innovation Valleys projects (funded under Horizon Europe and the I3 Instrument)
promising to accelerate innovation in connected regional innovation ecosystems across the EU.
Supporting SMEs, strengthening the Single Market and consumers’ rights
The agency will focus on unleashing the full potential of the Single Market through its three
flagships Enterprise Europe Network (EEN), Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs (EYE), Joint Cluster
Initiatives (EUROCLUSTERS), while continuing its support of consumer organisations and bodies.
Building up an efficient and purpose-driven agency
Internally, EISMEA will continue to enhance its environmental responsibility through implementing
its greening strategy, and build on staff engagement through initiatives such as staff visits to local
beneficiaries, fostering a greater understanding of the impact of EISMEA’s work.
4

PART 1. Mission statement
From ideas to global markets: Innovation made in Europe.
The European Innovation Council and Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Executive Agency
(EISMEA) was established on 1 April 2021 (1). With a focus on innovation and the single market, it
will create strong synergies to support the recovery, strengthening and twin transition of the
European economy. The agency has been entrusted with the implementation of the following (parts
of) Union programmes:
• Horizon Europe, pillar III: the European Innovation Council (EIC) and European Innovation
Ecosystems (EIE);
• European Regional Development Fund: Interregional Innovation Investments (I3)
Instrument;
• Single Market Programme: SME Pillar; Internal market; support to standardisation; and
Consumer Protection Pillar.
By implementing these programmes and specific delegated tasks (2), the agency will help unleash
the full potential of the single market and contribute to reaching the European Commission’s
objective of a new plan for Europe’s sustainable prosperity and competitiveness. In particular, it
will help to make sure that Europe’s open strategic autonomy is ensured and contribute to the
objectives of the STEP Regulation (3) to stimulate investments in critical technologies.
EISMEA’s mission is to provide high quality support to European innovators, researchers,
businesses, regions and consumers. We aim to reinforce the European Union’s position as a global
leader in Research and Innovation, strengthen its Single Market, open up opportunities for SMEs
and maintain high standards of protection for its citizens towards a more competitive, digital, green
and inclusive EU.
The agency implements its mission in close cooperation with its six parent DGs who are represented
on EISMEA’s Steering Committee:
• DG Research and Innovation (DG RTD),
• DG Communications Networks, Content and Technology (DG CONNECT),
• DG Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs (DG GROW),
• DG Justice and Consumers (DG JUST), DG Regional and Urban Policy (DG REGIO) and
• DG Mobility and Transport (MOVE).
It also benefits from the presence of Secretariat-General (SG) and of Directorate A of DG RTD as
Observers in the Steering Committee. This close cooperation is essential not only for programme
implementation tasks but also for the feedback the agency provides to the Commission in view of
the latter's policy tasks.

PART 3. Delivering on the Commission’s
priorities: main outputs for 2026
Horizon Europe
As part of Horizon Europe – the EU’s research and innovation framework programme – pillar 3
(Innovative Europe), the agency will implement actions under European Innovation Council and
European Innovation Ecosystems.
By implementing these actions EISMEA will help accelerate the conversion of emerging research
into transformative innovation that is commercialised and scaled up in the EU, while strengthening
digital and frontier technologies for Europe’s strategic autonomy. In doing so, EISMEA will
contribute to the European Commission’s objective ‘A new plan for Europe’s sustainable prosperity
and competitiveness.’
European Innovation Council (EIC)
The EIC aims to support the rapid scale up of innovative technologies and companies (mainly start-
ups and SMEs) at EU and international level. It is organised into three main funding schemes:
• the EIC Pathfinder for advanced research to develop the scientific basis to underpin
breakthrough technologies;
• the EIC Transition to validate and test technologies and plan a pathway to market; and
• the EIC Accelerator to help companies bring their innovations to market and scale up.
The financial support is complemented with access to Business Acceleration Services (BAS).
In addition, EIC prizes and other related actions, provide complementary support to promising
innovators. As well as implementing this funding and support, EISMEA also supports the European
Commission in its coordination of the activities of the EIC Board.
EIC Programme Managers
The priorities of the EIC Programme Managers for 2026 are as follows:
• Handover of EIC portfolios from six outgoing Programme Managers whose contract with
EISMEA will end in 2026 to six new Programme Managers.
• Awareness-raising of the Challenges of the EIC Work Programme 2026 among potential
applicants, helping to build a community that can respond to the relevant calls for
proposals. Activities include the (co-)organisation of info days: the EIC WP 2026 Challenges
developed by the Programme Managers for Pathfinder, Advanced Innovation and
Accelerator Challenges, as well as workshops and engagement with national contact points
(NCP).
7

• Development of Challenges for the EIC Work Programme 2027 in collaboration with the
parent DGs.
• Pro-active portfolio management for 25 Pathfinder Challenges coming from the 2021,
2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 Work Programmes, including the development and update of
their respective portfolio strategy plans.
• Participation in selection panels and juries for Pathfinder, Transition, Advanced Innovation
and Accelerator topics coming from the Work Programme 2026.
• Feedback to policy workshops with relevant DGs will be run by each Programme Manager
with relevant policy DGs and their impact measured via satisfaction surveys (see KPI table
above).
• Contribution to the EIC Impact Report and EIC Tech Report 2026.
EIC Pathfinder
The EIC Pathfinder offers grants to achieve proof of principle and validate the scientific basis of
breakthrough technology. EIC Pathfinder projects are characterised by their interdisciplinary /
multidisciplinary nature. In 2026, the agency will launch one “Open” call and three “Challenges”
(thematic calls) in the following areas:
• Advanced Materials for Miniaturised Energy Harvesting Systems,
• Biotechnology for Healthy Ageing,
• DeepRAP: Deep Reasoning, Abstraction & Planning towards trustworthy Cognitive AI
Systems.
These calls will offer grants up to EUR 4 million (Open and Challenges), or more if duly justified.
Put together, the calls will help accelerate the conversion of emerging research into transformative
innovation that is commercialised and scaled up in the EU, while strengthening digital and frontier
technologies for Europe’s strategic autonomy.
In addition, the agency will implement the 443 projects selected under the EIC Pathfinder calls
within Horizon Europe to date as well as the related legacy activities of the Horizon 2020
Programme Future and Emerging Technologies (FET) – around 95 grants. The agency will amend
a number of EIC Pathfinder projects by adding participants from widening countries that were
selected via the “Hop-on facility” call.
Further information is available in the annexed EIC Pathfinder performance table.
EIC Transition
The EIC Transition funds innovation activities that go beyond the experimental proof of principle in
laboratory. It targets research teams, established SMEs and spin-off companies willing to bring
closer to the market research results stemming from Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe eligible
projects.
The agency will launch one Transition call in 2025 that is open to any scientific and application
topic, offering around 40 grants of up to EUR 2.5 million to single applicants or small consortia.
Successful applicants must validate and demonstrate a technology in an application-relevant
8

environment and develop its market readiness. EIC Transition is open for proposals from European
Research Council Proof of Concept (ERC PoC) and Pillar II of Horizon Europe to Joint Undertakings
and Research Infrastructure, demonstrating synergies with other parts of Horizon Europe.
Implementing EIC Transition actions supports the Commission’s priority of putting research and
innovation (R&I) at the heart of the European economy, helping to accelerate the conversion of
emerging research into transformative innovation that is commercialised and scaled up in the EU,
while strengthening digital and frontier technologies for Europe’s strategic autonomy.
Further information is available in the annexed EIC Transition performance table
EIC Accelerator
The EIC Accelerator focuses on innovations building on scientific discovery or technological
breakthroughs (‘deep tech’) and where significant funding is needed over a long timeframe before
returns can be generated (‘patient capital’). Funding and support from the EIC Accelerator are
designed to enable such innovators attract the full investment amounts needed for scale up in a
shorter timeframe.
To implement the EIC Accelerator, the agency runs continuously open calls as well as specific
challenges, targeting EU policy priorities including the future proposals for European Biotech Act II,
Quantum Act, Advanced Materials Act, Cloud and AI Development Act (4), as well as concerning
critical technologies for the EU’s economic security (5). In 2026, the agency will manage an “Open”
call (continuously open for short proposals, with six batches through the year for full proposals),
and launch five “Challenges” (thematic calls) in the following areas:
• advanced materials for renewable energy and energy storage system;
• alternative concepts and key enabling technologies for fusion power plants;
• biotech for regenerating agricultural soils;
• boosting the European critical raw materials value chain; and
• deep tech for climate adaptation .
EISMEA will continue to select (with the help of external experts) the beneficiaries of EIC
Accelerator support, carry out technical due diligence with the help of experts, manage the grant
component and ensure coordination between the grant and investment components.
The agency will also continue to implement legacy activities (Fast Track to Innovation, SME
Instrument and EIC Pilot projects) launched under Horizon 2020 as well as more than 470 ongoing
grants under Horizon Europe. EISMEA will implement its responsibilities in relation to the EIC Fund
along with its lead parent DG (DG RTD) and with the other implementing parties (EIB, AlterDomus
(Fund Manager) and AlterDomus (administrator)) according to the third Commission Decision of

Strengthening the EIC: additional calls
In addition to the three pillars of the EIC (Pathfinder, Transition and Accelerator), the EIC foresees
several complementary initiatives in 2026 addressing specific political objectives.
Pilot EIC Advanced Innovation Challenges
In 2026 EISMEA will manage this pilot call under Horizon Europe that aims to support high-risk,
demand-driven deep tech innovation with transformative potential especially in areas where there
is extensive research but a lack of commercial uptake.
Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP) scale-up call
In 2026 EISMEA will continue to manage the EIC Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP)
Scale Up Call which seeks to stimulate groundbreaking innovation in strategic technologies,
propelling Europe's economic, industrial, and technological competitiveness.
EIC Pre-Accelerator call
EISMEA also manages the EIC Pre-Accelerator call, offering grants between EUR 300,000 to EUR
500,000. The call aims to increase the innovation potential of early-stage deep tech startups in
widening countries to create a pipeline of projects for the Accelerator, helping them to attract
private investments and to scale up.
Support for Ukrainian tech SMEs and startups
EISMEA manages the support to Ukrainian tech SMEs in the form of EIC grants between
EUR 300,000 to EUR 500,000. The action supports Ukrainian tech SMEs and start-ups and SMEs
to enable them to better attract private investments, deploy innovations on the market, and scale
up.
Women TechEU initiative
EISMEA will implement a new EUR 15 million Coordination and Support Action (CSA) to continue
implementing the Women TechEU initiative. The consortium will provide support to third parties in
the form of grants of EUR 75 000. The initiative is designed to support early-stage women-led
deep-tech startups, paving their way for participation in future EIC calls.
Further information is available in the annexed EIC Additional Calls performance table.

EIC Prizes
EIC Prizes are a powerful tool to support and foster innovation. They engage with citizens by
shedding light on the best innovators and their practices while also having a direct impact on the
ecosystems and their players. The agency will pay the Award winners of the 2026 edition of the
European Capital of Innovation Awards (iCapital) and the 2026 edition of the EU Prize for Women
Innovators.
The Agency will also manage the process for:
The 2027 European Capital of Innovation Awards (iCapital) that recognise the role of cities as
catalysers of the local innovation ecosystem and stimulate new activities to boost game-changing
innovation.
The 2027 EU Prize for Women Innovators that celebrates and supports talented women
entrepreneurs from the EU and countries associated to Horizon Europe whose disruptive
innovations are driving positive changes for the people and the planet.
Further information is available in the annexed EIC Prizes performance table
EIC Community and Business Acceleration Services
The EIC’s Business Acceleration Services (BAS) use the pan-European reach of the EIC to
connect EIC beneficiaries, Seal of Excellence companies Women Tech EU, Pre-Accelerator and
Ukraine call beneficiaries with ecosystem and business partners. The objective is to stimulate the
development of the innovations as well as the growth of supported companies.
To do so, EISMEA deploys coaches and manages contracts and grants delivering value-added
services, such as 1-to-1 investment readiness support and access to business partners, corporates,
innovation procurers and investors. Initiatives include events, visits, access to overseas trade fairs,
global business expansion missions, pilots and trial collaborations to facilitate the international
expansion of EIC beneficiaries. The provision of these activities will be renewed with increased
budget through two new tender procedures to be launched in 2026.
All BAS services are accessible through the EIC Community platform which also offers peer-to-
peer activities, including a Women Leadership Programme and traineeship programme for
researchers to work in startups and gain entrepreneurship skills. In 2026 the agency will further
stimulate the uptake of services offered by selected ecosystem partners (including EIT KICs) in the
online catalogue by offering financial support to cover up to 50% of the costs for EIC beneficiaries.
It will also provide EIC beneficiaries with tailored services to enhance their capabilities to take part
in innovation procurement bids and will provide financial support for pilots between EIC
beneficiaries and public and private procurers. Pathfinder and Transition beneficiaries will benefit
from a continued set of venture building and training activities. The most promising companies -
in line with the STEP strategic domains - will receive scaleup support through the EIC Scaling Club
programme (a specific action within the New European Innovation Agenda). These activities will be
renewed through two calls for proposals and one call for tenders to be launched in 2026.
Further information is available in the annexed EIC Community and BAS performance table
11

European Innovation Ecosystems (EIE)
The agency is responsible for implementing European Innovation Ecosystems’ calls for proposals
and monitoring successful projects. In 2026, the calls will align with the EU Startup and Scaleup
Strategy, and support the completion of the New European Innovation Agenda (NEIA) Flagships,
with a specific focus on:
• Interconnected Innovation Ecosystems: The agency will continue to implement efficient,
inclusive, and interconnected innovation ecosystems across the EU, enhancing synergies and
cooperation between them, and supporting the creation and development of common
knowledge assets, for example, within regional innovation valleys.
• New competitiveness-driven topics such as the “European startup and scaleup hubs pilot” and
“From lab to market: strengthening the role of Technology Transfer Offices” will build upon the
EU’s strategic vision outlined in the EU Competitiveness Compass, the EIC scaling strategy, and
the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy They will contribute to the strengthening Europe’s deep
tech capabilities, increasing regional innovation cohesion and supporting the growth of globally
competitive companies.
The agency will also launch and implement procurement actions that support programme
objectives articulated in the NEIA, such as:
• European Assistance for Innovation Procurement
• Mapping of European philanthropic organisations
• Renewal of Benchmarking of national policy frameworks and investments on innovation
procurement across Europe
• Renewal of the EU Intellectual Property Helpdesk.
Further information is available in the annexed European Innovation Ecosystems performance
table
Single Market Programme
The agency will implement several complementary strands of the Single Market Programme: the
Consumer protection pillar (actions aimed at protecting the rights of consumers in the internal
market); the SME pillar (actions to support the competitiveness of SMEs), as well as actions
designed to strengthen the internal market and provide support to standardisation. The actions
reinforce the Commission’s focus on unleashing the full potential of the Single Market (7).
In implementing the actions outlined below, EISMEA will help to ensure that the Single Market is
more integrated. In line with the Single Market Strategy, this will contribute to enabling companies
to scale up and compete globally while driving industrial innovation and strengthening supply
chains. It will also help to ensure a prosperous and competitive tourism eco-system that creates
opportunities for businesses, while ensuring that consumers are empowered and better protected.
(7) 2026 Commission work programme https://commission.europa.eu/publications/2026-commission-work-

As such it will contribute to achieving the European Commission’s objectives of a new plan for
Europe’s sustainable prosperity and competitiveness, as well as supporting people, and
strengthening our societies and our social models.
Consumer protection pillar of the Single Market
Programme
The agency will be responsible for implementing grants to:
• Support the consumer organisations and bodies.
• Support individual consumers policy initiatives and objectives.
It will also be responsible for procurement in areas such as:
Market surveillance and enforcement including:
• joint actions (“Coordinated Activities on the Safety of Products”) to support the exchanges
of EU Member States and EEA EFTA enforcement officials notified to the European
Commission for the purposes of CPC Regulation (EU) 2017/2394;
• actions to support the capacity building of consumer protection enforcement authorities
responsible for the enforcement of consumer law for projects.
Capacity building and education including:
• consumer education and awareness raising, preparation and implementation of innovative
tools and collaborative programmes, in relation to the enforcement of consumer rights
and products safety as well as to support the implementation of the General Product
Safety Regulation (GPSR).
Studies, analyses and surveys including:
• consumers’ attitudes, behaviours, and experiences with respect to domestic and cross-
border trade, awareness of consumer rights and product safety, handling of consumer
complaints, and unfair commercial practices.
Events and external communication including the Consumer Summit, High-level
Ministerial/Presidency meetings, and Info Days.
By implementing these delegated actions, the agency will contribute to improving the
empowerment and protection of consumers.
In addition, the agency will finalise procedures planned under the 2025 Work Programme.
Further information is available in the annexed Consumer protection pillar performance table
SME pillar of the Single Market Programme
The agency will continue to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainability of SMEs by
implementing grants for the three flagships Enterprise Europe Network (EEN), Erasmus for Young
Entrepreneurs (EYE), Joint Cluster Initiatives (EUROCLUSTERS) and for other actions focused on
support to SMEs scaling up and tourism.
13

It will also be responsible for public procurement for the International IP SME Helpdesks, the EU
Construction Sector Observatory and a project to facilitate access to mentors for entrepreneurs
facing insolvency.
The agency will implement actions of the SME pillar under the Single Market Programmes from
the work programmes 2021 to 2025, and the legacy activities of the COSME programme (2014-
2020).
In addition to the work under the Single Market Programme, the agency will also ensure the
implementation of pilot and preparatory actions, mainly in the areas of tourism, retail and
industrial permitting procedures, stemming from the European Parliament and delegated via the
parent DG. These include the first two editions of the European Capitals of Small Retail Awards.
Further information is available in the annexed SME pillar performance table
Internal Market and support to standardisation
The agency will implement grants and procurement actions aimed at promoting and supporting
market surveillance and standardisation activities, specifically through:
• The support of the establishment and functioning of Union testing facilities;
• The support to joint enforcement actions by Market Surveillance Authorities;
• The development of high-quality standards and standardisation deliverables;
• The enhancement of the involvement of stakeholders representing SMEs, consumers,
environmental interests, and trade unions in the standardisation process.
In addition, the agency will continue managing action grants, concluded in the period 2013 to 2020
under successive Framework Partnership Agreements with European standardisation organisations
CEN, CENELEC, and ETSI.
All activities and calls will be promoted via social media channels and info days.
Further information is available in the annexed Internal Market and support to standardisation
performance table
European Regional Development Fund
(ERDF)
Interregional Innovation Investments (I3) Instrument
The European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) aims to strengthen economic and social
cohesion in the European Union by correcting imbalances between its regions. The I3 Instrument
is implemented under the EU Cohesion Policy, that encourages regions and Member States to
enhance existing European value chains and/or develop new ones in less developed regions. By
implementing the I3 instrument, the agency will help to boost innovation through investments
14

related to research and digitalisation. It will thus contribute to the European Commission’s
objective of ‘a new plan for Europe’s sustainable prosperity and competitiveness’.
The I3 Instrument focuses on joint or complementary smart specialisation areas to accelerate
innovation creation and deployment in connected regional innovation ecosystems across the EU.
It provides financial and advisory support through strands 1 and 2. Investment Strands 1 and 2a
provide financial and advisory support to innovation actors (with Strand 2a focussing on
innovation diffusion in less developed regions). Strand 2b supports actions to increase the
capacity of regional innovation ecosystems in less developed regions.
In 2026, EISMEA will implement the I3 instrument as follows:
• Monitor ongoing projects from previous calls including the ten projects under the Regional
Innovation Valleys initiative (the cornerstone of flagship 3 of the New European
Innovation Agenda).
• Evaluate and perform grant agreement preparations.
• Continue to monitor the new ‘I3 Support Facility’, a technical assistance supporting
innovation actors from less developed regions to participate in and implement I3
Instrument projects and provide policy feedback on the actions’/projects’ impact.
• Meet with project coordinators/beneficiaries (in the framework of the I3 Support Facility:
e.g. during the annual I3 Forum).
• Analyse the results and technological/economic regional impact of the funded projects
(policy feedback)
• Perform diverse I3 Instrument promotion activities and organise related events such as
dedicated info days for applicants.
Further information is available in the Interregional Innovation Investments performance table
15

PART 4. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework (8) supports sound management and decision-making. It notably
ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable levels
through cost-effective controls.
EISMEA has established an internal control system tailored to its particular characteristics and
circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal control system will be assessed on an
ongoing basis throughout the year and will be subject to a specific annual assessment covering all
internal control principles.
A. Human resource management
In 2026, EISMEA will continue building on the progress and success of its recovery plan, fostering
a transparent and supportive organisational culture. The focus will be on sustaining the upward
trend of the staff engagement index (from 58% in 2023 to 72% in the 2025 mid-term survey)
through various learning initiatives for staff and managers. Actions include inter-agency initiatives
such as the secondment of Temporary Agents (TA 2f), non-violent communication training bytes, and
mini masterclasses dedicated to management. Additional targeted actions will be developed in early
2026 following the results of the staff survey and of a EISMEA staff consultation on training needs. In
addition, the introduction of the new interagency mediation network will contribute to a culture of
communication and peaceful conflict resolution.
EISMEA has adopted a competency framework that will be used in the agency’s selection
processes. Accompanied by an assessment tool, this framework will support colleagues in their
professional development and help them shape their own career.
The agency will also continue to participate in interinstitutional initiatives such as the DG/Executive
Agencies’ exchange programme, the Interinstitutional Job Shadowing scheme and the Interagency
Talent Programme open to all staff.
Shaping the agency’s organisational culture
The agency will continue implementing its internal communication strategy in 2026, putting a
strong emphasis on transparency, community and purpose. Activities will include:
• Frequent “open door” slots and coffee chats for staff with senior management as well as
Town Hall meetings to encourage open and transparent exchanges.
• Visits for staff to local EISMEA beneficiaries to foster a greater understanding of the impact
of EISMEA’s work.

• Support for bottom-up initiatives and organisation of internal events to bring colleagues

2026 Staff allocation and Full Time Equivalent (FTEs) reduction
According to the revised Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) and Specific Financial Statement (SFS),
EISMEA will undergo a workforce reduction of 20 Full-Time Equivalents (FTEs) in 2026. However,
EISMEA will also receive 5 additional FTEs funded by contributions from Third Countries. The net
reduction will thus be 15 FTEs for 2026.
This reduction will be aligned with the allocation by delegated programme, while ensuring a
balance between activity types: approximately 86% dedicated to operational activities and 14% to
horizontal activities.
EISMEA will continue to plan and anticipate a further reduction of 21 FTEs in 2027. This will mainly
be accomplished by freezing vacant positions.
Promoting gender balance
The agency continues to work closely with the parent DGs, providing regular overview of the
situation, to maintain the balanced representation (9) in middle management positions, aiming to
maintain a good gender balance.
Further information is available in the annexed HR Management performance table
B. Digital transformation and data management
In 2026 EISMEA will continue to drive digital transformation and enhance data management,
aligning with the Commission’s Digital Strategy and IT security strategy, working towards the
following goals.
To foster a digital culture the agency will focus on developing digital skills by offering targeted
IT training. It will enhance, cybersecurity awareness including through an inter-agency cyber-
security awareness week. The agency will also continue to actively promote the use of M365 and
Microsoft TEAMS.
To enhance business-driven digital transformation, the agency will foster synergies with other
Commission departments to reuse and publish data, promoting the use of corporate data services
and ensuring interoperability. This will include an active collaboration track on EIC Taxonomies. It
will also work on increasing AI technical capabilities by promoting AI training to staff and
encouraging the use of Commission-wide AI solutions like GPT@EC.
To ensure a seamless digital environment, EISMEA will adopt a Reuse-Buy-Build approach for
embedding newer technologies and ensure all information systems are properly mapped for
(9) The responsibility for making these appointments lies with the parent DG
17

strategic fitness. It will prioritise the reuse of existing IT solutions, foster open-source software
practices, and encourage the use and sharing of code on code.europa.eu. To better align with IT
governance policies of the Commission, EISMEA will follow a detailed IT Governance policy for
Delegated IT Systems developed with parent DGs and will test the new approach with at least one
pilot by end-2026.
To remain green, secure and resilient, EISMEA will adopt the Eco-Management and Audit
Scheme and promote sustainable practices and technologies, such as paperless, energy efficiency
and promoting the use of Green Public Procurement Criteria (GPPC). It will work to ensure that its
IT security plans are updated.
The agency will continue to actively monitor compliance with the Data Protection Regulation (EU)
N° 2018/1725 and update its Data protection action plan when required, largely based on the
Action Plan of the Commission (C(2020) 7625) and the IAS recommendations on processing of
personal data. The agency’s Data Protection Officer will provide regular awareness and training
opportunities to staff and management, e.g. during the European Data Protection Day, and update
internal rules and guidelines, if required.
In 2026 the agency will continue its efforts to raise awareness on the handling of data breaches,
data subject rights, international transfers, obligations of Data controllers to update Data
Protection Notices (DPNs) and publish records, and recall that appropriate agreements with
Commission Services and external service providers should be in place as well as appropriate
resources to ensure compliance with data protection obligations.
Data Management
The Agency will work to enhance its data maturity level from “basic” to “developing” across four
key areas, following guidance from central services and under the supervision of its Local Data
Correspondent (LDC):
Data Management – Key activities will include the mapping of the Agency’s key data assets.
Ownership and Responsibilities – the Agency will assign data owners and stewards for key

C. Sound financial management
EISMEA continues to implement simplified cost options, including lump sums, with a view to
simplifying and making its procedures more efficient.
EISMEA applies cost-effective control procedures, guided by its recently updated Control Strategy,
to ensure the proper implementation of delegated programmes and the legality and regularity of
financial transactions, in line with the principle of sound financial management and effective
protection of the Union's financial interests.
The agency will monitor the implementation of the Internal Control Framework based on updated
Internal Control Monitoring Criteria and implement actions identified following the 2025 Internal
Control Assessment exercise to further improve its Internal Control Systems. In the second quarter
of the year, the agency will review the risks identified in relation to programme implementation in
2026 and at the end of the year it will conduct its 2027 annual risk assessment exercise. As part
of its ongoing risk management, the agency will closely monitor the implementation of SUMMA
(the Commission’s corporate finance system introduced in 2025), with a view to minimising risks
of delays of financial operations relating to the migration of data from the previous system and
technical failures.
To raise awareness among staff on key topics including the implementation of the risk assessment
exercise and the appropriate use of exception reporting, the agency will provide training and
information sessions for staff on different aspects of Internal Control, supported by an internal
network of colleagues. Furthermore, it will continuously monitor, assess and report to the
management on the implementation of action plans related to risk assessment and exception
reporting.
The agency will continue to implement its ex-post audit strategy for the delegated programmes
under the Single Market Programme (SMP) and the Interregional Innovation Investments (I3)
Instrument.
For Horizon 2020 (H2020) and Horizon Europe (HORIZON), the Common Audit Service (CAS) of the
Common Implementation Centre (CIC) carries out financial audits on grants based on actual costs,
including those concerning grants managed by the agency. EISMEA will continuously monitor and
report on the progress of CAS audits and support the CAS as required. For HORIZON lump sum
grants, the agency will carry out ex-post technical reviews based on guidance from the CAS.
Finally, the agency will regularly update its internal guidance and the Manual of Procedures to
ensure adequate coverage and dissemination of the relevant rules, processes and procedures.
Further information is available in the annexed Sound Financial Management performance table.
D. Fraud risk management
The agency will complete the implementation of its Anti-Fraud Strategy (adopted in 2023) and will
carry out a full revision of its strategy to ensure its continued effectiveness. The agency will also
contribute to the implementation of the Common Anti-Fraud Strategy in the Research and
19

Innovation Family and to the revised Commission Anti-Fraud strategy Action Plan (11). The agency
will undertake the following anti-fraud activities:
• Strengthen anti-fraud capacity through training, including mandatory sessions for newcomers,
to reinforce prevention and detection of potential fraud cases.
• Enhance responsiveness in case of suspicion of fraud by taking timely precautionary measures
and timely notifications of cases to OLAF.
• Cooperate closely with OLAF by providing timely and complete information to support handling
of selections and investigations.
• Reinforce monitoring mechanisms to ensure effective follow-up on recoveries, penalties and
other corrective measures in cases of fraud.
• Actively participate in the Fraud Prevention and Detection Network to contribute to the design
and implementation of the anti-fraud measures across the Commission.
• Actively participate in the Fraud and Irregularities in Research Committee as a platform for
exchanging best practices on fraud prevention, detection and correction.
• Contribute to the working group collecting user requirements to enhance a corporate risk-
scoring tool.
Further information is available in the annexed Fraud Risk Management performance table
E. Sound environmental management
EISMEA will continue to enhance its sustainability and environmental responsibility in line with the
Commission’s Communication on Greening the Commission (C(2022)2230).
In particular, the agency will continue implementing its own Greening Strategy and Action Plan
while working towards its target of reducing its emissions from staff professional travel through
close monitoring and awareness-raising in line with the Commission’s 2025-2029 strategic plan.
Initiatives planned for 2026 include:
• Engaging with EMAS initiatives and campaigns complemented by agency / inter-agency
greening initiatives such as Inter-agency Green Week.
• Following BEST (Building Energy Saving Together) actions by closing EISMEA’s building during
summer and winter holiday periods.
• Implementing the EC Guidelines for sustainable meetings and events.
Further information is available in the annexed Sound Environmental Management performance
table.
